text: What should I build for this hackathon?
My notes are a mess. I've tried every app and they all give me a list. Lists don't work for me because my brain doesn't go in a line.
What if the app just listened and figured out the structure? Like, I talk, and it sorts what I'm saying into topics.
That's the idea. A thread map. Each topic is a thread, tangents branch off, and it tracks where I left off.
Oh speaking of which I also need to email Professor Chen about the extension before Friday.
And the laundry. I keep forgetting. The dryer has been sitting there since—
Anyway for the hackathon, the placement needs to be fast. Like under three seconds. Otherwise it feels broken.
I should use the Muse Spark model. It supports JSON schema so I can get structured placement without parsing.
Wait, what was I saying? About the laundry?
Right, the dryer. I need to fold that tonight before it wrinkles. Done.
For the refiner, I want it to tidy things up in the background. Better titles, merge duplicate threads, pull out action items.
And it should work with Apple Reminders. If I say I need to do something by a date, one tap sends it to the real app.
I need to submit the project by November third. That's the deadline.
Maybe memory palace pictures too. Each thread gets a little illustration so I can find it by sight instead of reading every title.
Okay, so the stack is Rust for the backend, React for the UI, WebSocket for real-time, and four Muse models: Transcribe, Spark for placement, Spark for refining, and Image for the pictures.
The whole point is that I can think out loud and the app does the organizing. I don't have to stop and file things. I just talk.
